analysis: The supplied PR changes are documentation-only: CHANGELOG.md (head text excerpts only, no patch shown, so exact edits are not visible) and a one-line CONTRIBUTING.md patch bumping the documented Go toolchain from 1.25.0 to 1.25.7 (CONTRIBUTING.md line 42). No executable code, protocol, authorization, attestation, encryption, or billing logic is touched in the visible units. The CHANGELOG text describes SSD prefix cache behavior (default 100 GiB ceiling limited to half available disk, encrypted checkpoints). This is a narrative claim; it does not itself alter T-041/SEC-035 behavior, and the canonical threat model still states a fixed 'no ceiling' policy, so a documentation drift exists but there is no new vulnerability. Coverage limit: the CHANGELOG hunk lacked a diff, so unit 12/13 were reviewed as whole-file head text and any changed lines are not individually identified. The underlying code changes described by the CHANGELOG (SSD checkpoints, native paged KV, heartbeat telemetry, cache routing) are not in this batch and were not examined. The Go version bump relates to the toolchain, which likely moves with go.mod/mise.toml changes not supplied here; those could carry security relevance (stdlib fixes) but are not visible. The threat model may eventually need updating for the 100 GiB cap description (T-041 mitigation text says no fixed ceiling) if that code change landed in a different batch.
